brief_summary: Five-row by five-column matrix comparing full-size, TKL, 75%, 65%, and 60% keyboard layouts across numpad, function row, navigation cluster, arrow cluster presence, and approximate key count. Filled amber dots mark dedicated-key clusters, half-filled dots mark compressed/partial clusters, open dashed circles mark clusters removed entirely and pushed to a firmware layer.
data_sources: keyboard-layout-sizes-buying-guide.mdx § 'The five sizes, and what each one removes' — 'A full-size board runs roughly 104 keys — the alpha block, a function row, a navigation cluster ... a dedicated arrow cluster, and a full numeric keypad'
keyboard-layout-sizes-buying-guide.mdx § 'The five sizes, and what each one removes' — '**TKL** removes only the numpad, landing around 87 keys'

keyboard-layout-sizes-buying-guide.mdx § 'The five sizes, and what each one removes' — '**75%** removes the numpad and compresses the function row, nav cluster, and arrows ... typically landing in the low-to-mid 80s'
keyboard-layout-sizes-buying-guide.mdx § 'The five sizes, and what each one removes' — '**65%** removes the function row entirely, along with most of the navigation cluster ... around 66-68 keys'
keyboard-layout-sizes-buying-guide.mdx § 'The five sizes, and what each one removes' — '**60%** removes the function row, the full navigation cluster, and the arrow cluster ... around 61 keys'
